title: Ice Age People Traveled and Mixed More Than We Thought
summary:
More than 30,000 years ago, during the Ice Age, people in Europe were much more connected than scientists used to think. New DNA evidence shows that groups living far apart actually mixed with each other.

A team led by the University of Vienna studied ancient DNA from rare human remains and even from dirt in caves.

One important discovery came from a woman who lived about 30,000 years ago in what is now southwestern France. Most of her DNA was from western Europe, but some of it matched people from central and eastern Europe. Scientists think these groups mixed about 32,500 to 31,500 years ago — much earlier than anyone knew.

Other groups stayed in one place for thousands of years. DNA from caves in Spain shows that people sheltered there during the coldest part of the Ice Age.

"Our results show that eastern and western European populations were not as genetically isolated as previously assumed," said researcher Pere Gelabert.
why_it_matters: This story is about family history too — it shows people have always traveled and mixed with faraway groups.
